syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Introduction to computer system: CPU, input and output devices

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the role of the CPU, its registers, ALU and control unit.
Identify input and output devices and how data entered is stored.
Recall key inventions from the abacus to the tabulating machine.
Explain the stored program concept and Von Neumann architecture.
Relate LSI, VLSI, SLSI and Moore's Law to the growth of computing power.
Convert between bits, nibbles, bytes and larger memory units.
Distinguish RAM and ROM by volatility and use.
Explain the role of cache memory and compare secondary memory with primary memory.

topics.title: Data transfer between memory and CPU

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the data, address and control buses and their direction of transfer.
Describe how the CPU reads from and writes to main memory over the system bus.
Interpret the generations of microprocessors and their memory sizes.
Explain word size, clock speed and cores of a microprocessor.
Distinguish a microcontroller from a microprocessor and give its uses.
Classify data as structured, unstructured or semi-structured.
Describe data capturing, storage and retrieval.
Explain how deleted data can be recovered and how to protect it.

topics.title: Software: system software, programming tools and application software

concepts.learning_objective: Identify operating systems, system utilities and device drivers as system software.
Distinguish low-level and high-level languages and the role of assembler, compiler and interpreter.
Classify application software and distinguish FOSS, freeware and proprietary software.
Describe the objectives of an operating system and its types of user interface.
Explain process, memory, file and device management by the operating system.
Explain how 7-bit ASCII maps keyboard characters to unique codes and binary values.
Describe ISCII as an 8-bit code that retains ASCII and adds Indian language characters.
Explain why UNICODE was developed and how it relates to ASCII.
Identify the common UNICODE encodings and represent a code point in binary.

topics.title: Number Systems: Decimal, Binary, Octal and Hexadecimal

concepts.learning_objective: State the base and symbols of the decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal number systems.
Determine the positional value of a digit in a number of any base.
Use hexadecimal notation for memory addresses and RGB colour codes.

topics.title: Conversion from Decimal to other Number Systems

concepts.learning_objective: Convert a decimal integer to binary, octal or hexadecimal by repeated division.

topics.title: Conversion from other Number Systems to Decimal

concepts.learning_objective: Convert binary, octal and hexadecimal integers to decimal using positional expansion.

topics.title: Conversion from Binary to Octal/Hexadecimal and Vice-Versa

concepts.learning_objective: Convert between binary and octal by grouping bits in threes.
Convert between binary and hexadecimal by grouping bits in fours.

topics.title: Conversion of a Number with Fractional Part

concepts.learning_objective: Convert a decimal fraction to binary by repeated multiplication by 2.
Convert numbers with fractional parts from other bases to decimal, octal or hexadecimal.

topics.title: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and NLP

concepts.learning_objective: Describe AI as simulating human cognitive functions using a knowledge base.
Explain how machine learning models are trained and tested on data to make predictions.
Identify applications of NLP such as predictive typing, speech-to-text and machine translation.
Distinguish virtual reality from augmented reality and give their applications.
Describe robots, their types and applications such as rovers, humanoids and drones.
Explain what big data is and why traditional tools cannot process it.
Identify the five Vs of big data: volume, velocity, variety, veracity and value.
Describe data analytics and its uses in business and science.

topics.title: Internet of Things, Web of Things, Sensors and Smart Cities

concepts.learning_objective: Define IoT as a network of devices with embedded hardware and software that exchange data.
Explain how WoT uses web services to connect IoT devices through one interface.
Describe the role of sensors, including smart sensors, in IoT and smart cities.
Explain cloud computing as on-demand, pay-per-use services delivered over the Internet.
Distinguish IaaS, PaaS and SaaS with examples.
Describe a grid as dispersed, heterogeneous nodes working together on a large task.
Identify data and CPU grids, middleware like Globus, and contrast grids with IaaS.
Explain blockchain as a decentralised, shared, append-only ledger kept by all nodes.
Evaluate applications of blockchain in currency, healthcare, land records and voting.
Identify the key steps of problem solving with a computer and their order.
Explain the role of testing, debugging and maintenance, including syntax versus logical errors.
Define an algorithm as a finite sequence of precise steps that produces the desired output.
Describe precision, uniqueness, finiteness, input and output as characteristics of a good algorithm.
Identify standard flowchart symbols and their functions.
Explain pseudocode, its keywords and its benefits.
Trace algorithms that execute in sequence or choose a branch based on a condition.
Trace loops with a counter and loops that repeat until a condition becomes false.
Use a dry run with suitable inputs to find incorrect or missing steps in an algorithm.
Compare algorithms for the same problem on processing time and memory used.
Distinguish high-level and low-level languages and the factors in choosing a language.
Explain how decomposition breaks a complex problem into sub-problems that are solved and integrated.

topics.title: Introduction to Python: features, interpreter and execution modes

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the main features of Python such as being high level, open source, portable and case-sensitive.
Explain how an interpreter executes a program statement by statement, unlike a compiler.
Distinguish between the interactive mode and the script mode of the Python interpreter.
Recognise Python keywords as reserved words that cannot be used as identifiers.
Apply the rules for naming identifiers to decide whether a name is valid.
Explain implicit variable creation by assignment and the use of # comments.

topics.title: Everything is an object and Python data types

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that every Python value is an object with a unique identity returned by id().
Identify the numeric types int, float, complex and bool from given values.
Describe strings, lists, tuples, sets, None and dictionaries and how they are written.

topics.title: Mutable and immutable data types and choosing a data type

concepts.learning_objective: Classify data types as mutable or immutable and trace what happens when a variable is updated.
Choose a suitable data type (list, tuple, set or dictionary) for a given situation.
Evaluate arithmetic and augmented assignment operators including %, // and **.
Evaluate relational comparisons, including string comparison, and logical operators.
Use the identity operators is, is not and the membership operators in, not in.

topics.title: Expressions, precedence of operators and statements

concepts.learning_objective: Identify valid expressions and statements in Python.
Evaluate expressions using operator precedence and left-to-right evaluation.
Use input() and print() with its sep and end parameters, knowing that input() returns a string.
Apply explicit type conversion with int(), float() and str() and predict its result.
Explain implicit conversion (coercion) and type promotion from int to float.

topics.title: Debugging: syntax, logical and runtime errors

concepts.learning_objective: Define debugging as the process of identifying and removing errors from a program.
Distinguish syntax errors, logical errors and runtime errors with examples.
Define flow of control and recognise sequence as statements executed in the order written.
Identify selection and repetition as the two control structures supported by Python.
Explain how if and if..else statements choose between blocks based on a condition.
Trace an if..elif..else chain to find which block executes.
Explain how Python uses indentation to form blocks and predict the effect of indentation on output.

topics.title: Repetition and the for loop with range()

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a loop's control variable and condition decide repetition and termination.
Trace a for loop to count the number of iterations.
Determine the sequence generated by range() with start, stop and step values.
Trace a while loop and determine the values of variables after it ends.
Recognise an infinite loop and explain why its condition never becomes false.
Explain how break terminates a loop and predict the resulting output.
Explain how continue skips the rest of an iteration and predict the resulting output.
Define a nested loop and count how many times its inner body executes.
Trace nested loops that print number patterns and prime numbers.
Define a function as a named group of instructions that performs a specific task when invoked.
Explain how functions improve readability, reduce code length and enable reuse and team work.

topics.title: Creating user defined functions: arguments and parameters

concepts.learning_objective: Write a correct function header using def, a name, parameters and a colon with an indented body.
Distinguish arguments in a call from parameters in a definition.
Apply the rule that default parameters must be trailing parameters.

topics.title: Functions returning values and flow of execution

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the return statement sends value(s) or None back to the caller.
Trace the order in which statements run when functions are defined and called.
Distinguish global and local variables and where each can be accessed.
Use the global keyword to modify a global variable inside a function.

topics.title: Built-in functions of the standard library

concepts.learning_objective: Identify and predict the output of commonly used built-in functions.

topics.title: Modules: math, random, statistics and user defined modules

concepts.learning_objective: Use import and from statements to access functions of a module.
Predict the results of common math, random and statistics module functions.
Create strings using single, double and triple quotes.
Access characters of a string using positive and negative indices.
Recognise when an out-of-range index raises IndexError.
Explain that the contents of a string cannot be changed after creation.
Apply the + and * operators to join and repeat strings.
Use in and not in to test for substrings.
Extract substrings with str[n:m], including omitted and negative indices.
Use a step size in slicing, including negative steps to reverse a string.
Traverse a string character by character with a for loop.
Traverse a string using a while loop, an index and len().
Use methods such as title(), upper() and lower() to change case.
Use find(), index() and count() to locate and count substrings.
Apply split(), join(), strip() and replace() to transform strings.

topics.title: Handling strings with user defined functions

concepts.learning_objective: Trace user defined functions that count or replace characters in a string.
Reverse a string with negative indices and check for palindromes.

topics.title: Introduction to lists: creating, accessing elements and mutability

concepts.learning_objective: Describe a list as an ordered, mutable sequence whose elements may be of different types.
Access list elements using positive and negative indices and recognise an out-of-range index.
Explain that list elements can be changed in place, unlike string characters.

topics.title: List operations: concatenation, repetition, membership and slicing

concepts.learning_objective: Use the + and * operators to join and repeat lists.
Evaluate the membership operators in and not in on lists.
Predict the result of list slices with start, stop and step, including negative steps.
Traverse a list with a for loop over its elements or over range(len(list)).
Traverse a list with a while loop and an index variable.
Distinguish append(), extend() and insert() and predict the resulting list.
Use remove() and pop() and predict their effect, including ValueError cases.
Apply count(), index(), sort(), sorted(), reverse(), len(), min(), max() and sum().
Access elements of a nested list using two indices.
Distinguish aliasing by assignment from copying by slicing, list() and copy.copy().

topics.title: List as argument to a function

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a function receiving a list can change the caller's list object.
Explain why assigning a new list to a parameter does not affect the caller's list.
Choose suitable list methods to implement a menu of list operations.
Trace programs that compute an average and perform a linear search on a list.

topics.title: Introduction to tuples: creation, indexing and immutability

concepts.learning_objective: Create tuples correctly, including a single-element tuple and a tuple without parentheses.
Access tuple elements using positive and negative indices.
Explain that a tuple cannot be changed after creation, though a mutable element inside it can.
Apply the + and * operators to tuples and predict the result.
Use in, not in and slicing on tuples.

topics.title: Tuple methods, built-in functions and tuple assignment

concepts.learning_objective: Use len(), tuple(), count(), index(), sorted(), min(), max() and sum() with tuples.
Assign the elements of a tuple to a tuple of variables and predict unpacking errors.
Store and access records in a nested tuple.
Use tuples to swap values, return multiple values and build a tuple in a loop.
Create a dictionary of key: value pairs and state the rules for keys.
Access dictionary values through keys and recognise KeyError.
Add and modify items in a dictionary.
Use membership operators on keys and traverse a dictionary with a for loop.
Use len(), dict(), keys(), values(), items(), get(), update(), del and clear().
Write and trace programs that process data stored in dictionaries.
Distinguish active digital footprints, submitted intentionally, from passive footprints left unintentionally.
Explain why digital footprints stored on servers cannot be guaranteed to be fully erased and can be used to trace a user.

topics.title: Digital Society, Netizen and Net Etiquettes

concepts.learning_objective: Define a netizen as anyone who uses digital technology with the Internet and state what being a good netizen means.
Apply the net etiquettes of being ethical, respectful and responsible, including avoiding cyber bullying and not feeding trolls.
Apply the communication etiquettes of being precise, polite and credible in digital communication.
Apply social media etiquettes of being secure and reliable, such as choosing passwords wisely and thinking before uploading.

topics.title: Data Protection and Intellectual Property Rights

concepts.learning_objective: Identify sensitive data and the methods used to protect its privacy.
Distinguish copyright, patent and trademark as ways of protecting intellectual property.

topics.title: Violation of IPR, Public Access and Open Source Software

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish plagiarism, copyright infringement and trademark infringement.
Describe Creative Commons, GNU GPL and FOSS, and explain why software piracy is copyright infringement.
Distinguish ethical (white hat) hacking from non-ethical (black hat) hacking.
Identify phishing, identity theft and ransomware from their features.
Choose safety measures that reduce the risk of cyber crime.

topics.title: Indian IT Act and Impact on Health

concepts.learning_objective: State the purpose and main provisions of the Information Technology Act, 2000, amended in 2008.
Explain how ergonomics and healthy habits reduce the physical and mental effects of overusing digital devices.
